title: Normalized factors and comparison coordinates of the relative product
statement: Fix the six-functor datum $S$ of [def-sf-datum] and the four coefficient-stage selectors of [def-sf-ctf-coefficient-stage-selectors]. Use the canonical partial finite tensor and supplied projection mates of [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates], the coefficient comparison data of [def-pur-finite-compact-support-scalar-data] and the canonical finite K-flat tensor models of [def-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Define a relative-product stage to be pullback on separated morphisms, compact-support functors on specified compactifications, and their supplied compositor. Define operation expressions generated from two input variables by these pullbacks, compact-support images and binary tensor, with evaluation as an actual bifunctor. For a compactified Cartesian square $(u,v,f,g)$ put $P=u^*K$, $Q=f_!K$, $H=P\otimes v^*L$, $h=vg$, and define the seven expressions $h_!H$, $g_!v_!H$, $g_!(v_!P\otimes L)$, $g_!(g^*Q\otimes L)$, $g_!(L\otimes g^*Q)$, $g_!L\otimes Q$, $Q\otimes g_!L$. Define their six successive factors from the supplied composition comparison, inverse projection at $(v,P,L)$, inverse exchange tensored with identity, signed symmetry, inverse projection at $(g,L,Q)$ and final signed symmetry. At each coefficient stage a normalized presentation is restriction of the actual operations to the finite-Tor full subcategories: its operation and tensor functors agree with the recorded functors after full inclusion, and its projection, exchange and symmetry maps agree with the recorded canonical maps. No existence is included in this definition. Define primitive coefficient comparison data by restricting the given operation comparisons and tensor comparison, retaining their forward A5 equations. Recursively define comparison isomorphisms on all expressions and the individual factor-square predicate. Define proper coordinates by the direct-image restrictions and the specified proper identifications after full inclusion; define replacements at any selected proper occurrences, their recursive object comparisons, and the corresponding proper exchange/projection normalization and factor-square predicates. Define admissible recorded coefficient comparison by normalization to the identity, finite quotient or ramified finite scalar change, integral scalar change, integral reduction, rationalization, finite-field transition, or inclusion into the algebraic closure. These are construction data and normalization predicates, not assertions of existence or commutativity of inverse-factor squares.
